translation.title: Nicotine Patch (Smoking Cessation Aid)
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used as an aid to smoking cessation.
translation.usage: Adults apply 1 patch once a day to a hairless part of the body (such as the buttock or the inner upper arm), changing the application site every day. Nicostop-30 is generally used by people who smoke 20 or more cigarettes a day, and Nicostop-20 by people who smoke up to 20 cigarettes a day. Nicostop-10 is used in the final stage to reduce nicotine replacement. Heavy smokers start with Nicostop-30, then move to Nicostop-20 and finally to Nicostop-10, using each for 4 weeks. Average smokers use Nicostop-20 for 8 weeks and then Nicostop-10 for 4 weeks. Treatment must not exceed 3 months.
translation.caution: If you keep smoking while using this medicine, cardiovascular side effects caused by nicotine may occur more often and more markedly, so it should be used only by people who have stopped smoking completely. Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, or if you have a chronic skin disease (psoriasis, chronic dermatitis, urticaria), a generalised skin disease, irritant dermatitis, unstable angina, worsening angina, a myocardial infarction within the past 3 months, the late phase of an acute infarction, severe cardiac arrhythmia, systemic hypertension, peripheral vascular disease, or cerebrovascular disease (acute stroke, cerebrovascular disorder). It must also not be used by women who are pregnant or breastfeeding, by children and adolescents under 18 years of age, or by non-smokers and occasional smokers. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before using this medicine if you have gastritis, peptic ulcer, occlusive arterial disease, stable angina, heart failure, decompensated heart failure, myocardial infarction, cardiac arrhythmia, vasospasm, uncontrolled hypertension, an arterial bypass graft or angioplasty, renal failure, hepatic failure, diabetes, hyperthyroidism, or phaeochromocytoma. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you use this medicine together with paracetamol, caffeine, imipramine, oxazepam, pentazocine, propranolol, theophylline, warfarin, oestrogens, lignocaine, phenacetin, insulin, adrenergic antagonists (such as prazosin or labetalol), flecainide, adrenergic agonists (such as isoprenaline or phenylephrine), propoxyphene, furosemide diuretics, H2 antagonists, beta blockers, tacrine, clozapine, or ropinirole. Stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist if you experience headache, dizziness, sleep disturbance, anxiety, emotional instability, agitation, abnormal dreams, confusion, restlessness, impaired concentration, fatigue, migraine, spasm, leg cramps, changes in blood pressure, hypertension, palpitations, nausea, abdominal pain, indigestion, constipation, diarrhoea, vomiting, gastric ulcer, difficulty swallowing, altered bowel habit, increased appetite, cold or influenza symptoms, cough, pharyngitis, rhinitis, sinusitis, upper respiratory symptoms, bronchitis, difficulty breathing, redness, swelling, allergy, rash, herpetiform eruption, itching, urticaria, acne, skin discolouration, taste disturbance, visual disturbance, dysmenorrhoea, muscle pain, joint pain, toothache, back pain, chest pain, general pain, earache, facial flushing, local swelling, weight gain, dry mouth, flatulence, gingivitis, thyroid dysfunction, lymph node pain, cystitis or increased sweating. Store at room temperature away from moisture and light, and keep out of reach of children.
